reading.title: The Science of Willpower
reading.intro_zh: 本篇是关于“自制力”的真实科普阅读，话题与本课“严格规则、诱惑与给自己找借口”相呼应。内容改编自美国心理学会（APA）的权威文章，介绍了棉花糖实验、意志力为何会被耗尽，以及如何抵抗诱惑。

source.title: What you need to know about willpower: The psychological science of self-control

passage: Psychologists define willpower as the capacity to resist immediate temptations in order to pursue more valuable long-term goals. The most famous demonstration of this struggle is the so-called marshmallow test, designed by Walter Mischel. Preschoolers were offered a simple but agonising choice: eat one treat at once, or wait alone for roughly fifteen minutes and receive two. Remarkably, the children who managed to delay gratification tended, decades later, to earn higher test scores and cope with stress more effectively. Mischel explained their success through two competing systems in the mind. A calm, rational "cool" system keeps distant goals in view, whereas an impulsive, emotional "hot" system reacts instantly to whatever tempting object happens to be in front of us.

Yet willpower is not an unlimited resource. Researchers have shown that deliberately resisting temptation drains a person's mental energy, so that someone who has just refused a plate of cookies performs worse on a demanding task afterwards. This phenomenon, known as depletion, is linked to a measurable drop in the brain's available glucose. Fortunately, self-control can be conserved and even strengthened. The most reliable tactic is surprisingly ordinary: keeping temptations physically out of sight, since workers who stored sweets inside a drawer ate far fewer than those who left them on the desk. People also resist more successfully when they prepare concrete "if-then" plans in advance and concentrate on a single goal rather than scattering their efforts across many at once.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The history of how marshmallows were invented and sold.
Why children should never be left alone with sweets.
What science reveals about how self-control works and can be improved.
How psychologists disagree about the value of long-term goals.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕“意志力（自制力）的科学”展开：先解释定义和棉花糖实验，再讲意志力会被耗尽，最后讲如何保存和增强自制力，所以主旨是科学如何揭示自制力的运作与改善方法。

questions.question: In the marshmallow test, what reward did children receive if they waited?
options: Two treats instead of one.
A higher test score on the spot.
Permission to leave the room early.
A choice between candy and a toy.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说孩子可以马上吃一个，或独自等大约十五分钟后得到两个（receive two），所以等待的奖励是两份零食而不是一份。

questions.question: According to the passage, why does someone perform worse on a task after refusing cookies?
options: Because the cookies made them physically ill.
Because they lost interest in the long-term goal.
Because the task itself had suddenly become harder.
Because resisting temptation drains their mental energy.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中指出刻意抵抗诱惑会消耗人的心理能量（drains a person's mental energy），所以刚拒绝了饼干的人随后在任务上表现更差，这就是“耗损”现象。

questions.question: What can we infer about the best way to avoid giving in to temptation?
options: Relying only on raw determination is the surest method.
Changing your environment can be more effective than sheer effort.
Pursuing many goals at once strengthens willpower fastest.
Keeping tempting objects nearby helps you practise resisting.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说最可靠的办法是把诱惑放到看不见的地方（抽屉里的糖比桌上的吃得少），并提前做计划、专注单一目标；这说明改变环境往往比单纯靠意志硬撑更有效。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "agonising" (in "a simple but agonising choice") most nearly means
options: extremely boring and dull.
easy and quickly decided.
causing intense difficulty or distress.
funny and lighthearted.
questions.explanation_zh: agonising 意为“令人极其痛苦、纠结的”。对孩子来说，立刻吃一个还是忍住等两个是一个让人非常煎熬的选择，所以指造成强烈困扰或痛苦。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把五个 Lesson 51 的“严格规则与内疚反应”句式提升到 B2+：用 hurriedly hid...under... 写出于心虚而迅速藏匿，用 First of all 引出计划的第一步，用 which were forbidden 描述被明令禁止的内容，用 It was obvious that 点出一望即知的情绪，最后用 so strict that 写规则严苛到产生某种结果或借口。

patterns.title: hurriedly hid ... under ...
patterns.source: He led me into his room and hurriedly hid a large parcel under his desk.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个句式用一个快速动作表现心虚或尴尬；hurriedly 说明动作很急，under 交代藏到哪里。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人在毫无防备时被人撞见，出于心虚或恐慌，慌忙把某样不该被看到的东西藏到别的物体下面。
patterns.sample: The moment the inspector walked in, the nervous clerk hurriedly hid the unfinished report under a pile of old newspapers.
patterns.tip_zh: 先写人，再写 hurriedly hid + 物品 + under + 地点；不要把 hurriedly 放到句尾。

patterns.title: First of all, ...
patterns.source: First of all, he wrote out a long list of all the foods which were forbidden.
patterns.focus_zh: First of all 用来写计划的第一步，后面接一个完整动作，让安排更有条理。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某个团队或机构在启动一项严肃计划时，第一步采取了什么有条理的、能约束后续行为的措施。
patterns.sample: First of all, the committee drew up a detailed budget so that no department could spend money without prior approval.
patterns.tip_zh: First of all 后面要加逗号，再写主语和动词。

patterns.title: a list of ... which were forbidden
patterns.source: He wrote out a long list of all the foods which were forbidden.
patterns.focus_zh: which were forbidden 是关系从句，用来说明 list 里的东西是不被允许的。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某个组织或场合公布了一张清单，明确列出在一段时期内被严格禁止的若干行为或物品。
patterns.sample: The new manager circulated a list of practices which were forbidden, ranging from personal calls to leaving early without notice.
patterns.tip_zh: which were forbidden 要紧跟它修饰的复数名词，比如 games, snacks, websites。

patterns.title: It was obvious that ...
patterns.source: It was obvious that he was very embarrassed.
patterns.focus_zh: It was obvious that 用来写“别人一眼就看得出来”的事实或情绪。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：通过具体的动作或细节，写出某人的紧张、尴尬、自豪或失落非常明显，旁人一眼就能看出。
patterns.sample: It was obvious that the candidate was struggling, for he kept rephrasing the same answer and avoiding the interviewer's eyes.
patterns.tip_zh: that 后面接完整句子；如果写情绪，常用 nervous, embarrassed, proud, excited。

patterns.title: so strict that ...
patterns.source: His diet was so strict that he had to reward himself occasionally.
patterns.focus_zh: so strict that 表示“严格到产生某个结果”，特别适合写规则过严带来的反应或借口。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一项学习、训练或工作安排严苛到了极点，以至于迫使某人不得不寻求休息、奖励或某种妥协。
patterns.sample: Her training schedule was so strict that even her coach quietly urged her to take an occasional day of rest.
patterns.tip_zh: so strict that 中间不要拆开；that 后面写结果，可以是 needed, had to, wanted to。
